answer: Imagine a harbor where each ship sails under one lantern, lit by a cipher only its own captain can turn. If a single captain flies that same lantern on ten hulls, the harbor master sees one light copied ten times and scuttles all ten together - joint slashing. One mistake burns a hundred bonds at once, so a farm of a hundred clones risks a hundredfold loss, while one honest ship keeps its lantern lit and sails on.
